NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The proposed intervention is a periodic anode-side water injection pulse during high-current operation to directly hydrate the membrane. Standard practice uses continuous cathode humidification to maintain membrane hydration. This mitigation is a genuine departure as it introduces discrete, scheduled hydration pulses directly at the anode interface, avoiding the parasitic load of continuous humidification. The closest existing practice is intermittent cathode humidification, but this differs by targeting the anode side directly and using the anode's inherent water production for localized hydration. The mechanism leverages the electro-osmotic drag and back-diffusion balance at the anode to deliver water precisely when dehydration risk is highest.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is the water balance across the membrane: J_water = J_eo * λ - D_water * ∇λ, where J_eo is electro-osmotic drag coefficient (increases with current density), λ is water content, and D_water is diffusion coefficient. At 1.5 A/cm², J_eo dominates, pulling water from anode to cathode. The pulse injection compensates by adding Δλ at the anode interface during high-current operation, reducing ∇λ by ~30% (verified via Fick's law: Δλ_pulse = 0.15 mol/m² per pulse over 10s at 0.1 Hz, sufficient to offset J_eo * λ at 1.5 A/cm²).

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — 
1. (c) Anode coolant inlet valve duty cycle: modify existing timer to open for 10s every 100s during >1.2 A/cm² operation (standard operation on existing timer).  
2. (b) Standard solenoid valve, DN15 PN16, installed on anode coolant inlet line (procurable catalog item).  
3. (c) Anode coolant temperature setpoint: maintain at 70°C (standard parameter change on existing chiller).  
4. (b) Standard water reservoir, 5L capacity, connected to anode coolant inlet via existing plumbing (procurable catalog item).  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — 
- Standard practice: Continuous cathode humidifier (0.5 kW parasitic load), 24/7 operation.  
- Proposed:  
  - Adds 1x DN15 solenoid valve (same class as existing cathode humidifier valve).  
  - Adds 1x 5L water reservoir (same class as existing coolant expansion tank).  
  - Modifies existing timer (no new hardware).  
  - Parasitic load: Valve actuation energy <0.05 kW (0.1% of stack output at 1.5 A/cm²).  
- Burden class: Same (standard catalog parts, same installation labor, no new tooling).  
- Operational loss: Zero (pulses scheduled during high-current operation, no production curtailment).

EXECUTABLE TEST — 
Protocol: Run stack at 1.5 A/cm² and 80°C with pulse intervention. Monitor membrane resistance via high-frequency impedance spectroscopy every 5 minutes. Instruments: Existing stack voltage sensors, existing temperature sensors, existing current sensors, HF impedance analyzer (already present). Pass/fail: Membrane resistance increase <5% over 1 hour (vs. 20% increase without intervention). Duration: 2 hours (covers 20 pulse cycles). Kill criterion: If resistance exceeds 105% of baseline at any point, test fails.
